hints.title: Deeply Nested Structure Traversal
hints.text: A stream contains integers nested arbitrarily deep inside recursive list containers. How can a deferred evaluation container maintain the current position across nested boundaries?

hints.title: Reverse-Pushed Evaluation Stack
hints.text: Push the elements of nestedList onto an internal stack in reverse order so that the first element sits at the top ready for evaluation.

hints.title: Lazy Unpacking in hasNext
hints.text: In hasNext, inspect the top element. If it is an integer, return true. If it is a list, pop it and push its contents back onto the stack in reverse order. Repeat until an integer is surfaced or stack empties.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(1) amortized per next and hasNext call
variables: D: maximum nesting depth of the list
complexity.notes: Each nested list and integer is pushed and popped at most once throughout iteration.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Flattening the entire nested structure up front during initialization consumes O(N) memory and fails to support infinite or lazy streams.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stack size is proportional to maximum nesting depth plus siblings, providing lazy on-demand streaming.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Performing lazy unpacking inside hasNext rather than eager recursion in the constructor.
